findings.problem: A downstream hypothesis/scope gap is represented as an unresolved presence event after that event was validated.
findings.proposedRepair: Use a qualified retained-assessment-gap ending that names which proposition remains unknown and preserves validated presence; evaluate that distinction rather than unconditionally answering unresolved yes.

findings.problem: Partial fileId-only scope inclusions can satisfy the full file/system source context.
findings.proposedRepair: Require all declared subject fields for each included/excluded/unknown entity; unresolved partial identity remains unknown and cannot satisfy a full source inclusion. Keep distinct systems distinct.

findings.problem: The base matcher treats a nominal timestamp as determinate even when supplied clock uncertainty crosses the investigation interval.
findings.proposedRepair: Require finite nonnegative clock uncertainty and full event-time interval containment, following the profile matcher; boundary overlap retains unknown.

findings.problem: Unavailable-content filtering uses only content.* and payload.* fact-name prefixes. An unavailable-byte hypothesis can still return yes from a manifest digest named file.sha256; metadata digest agreement is not independently acquired byte verification.
findings.proposedRepair: Declare each fact/criterion evidence dependency and acquisition basis. Preserve metadata-level digest statements while making current-content/byte-verification claims unknown unless independently acquired content is available in an explicitly bound context.

findings.problem: Historical lineage remains separate from file presence and bytes, but parentRevisionId is only a required present fact: a boolean is accepted as the named historical parent. Parent identity/type/namespace and observation-vs-relation-time interpretation need an explicit contract.
findings.proposedRepair: Require a named, typed parent revision identity in its declared namespace/context; reject nonidentities, preserve self-parent uncertainty and distinguish the observed manifest relation from independently established history/content.

findings.problem: Base routes introduce unrelated retention-focus predicates with no investigative discovery or context adapter. Open-focus bookkeeping does not supply a reason to turn content-lineage, ancestry or provenance evidence into another facet question.
findings.proposedRepair: Use an explicit source-focus-qualified or generic retained-assessment ending. Preserve the source focus and all separate answers; do not manufacture evidence or mandatory new investigative work merely to preserve historical topology.
findings.scenario: For Q56-no, a completed content-lineage search need not introduce data-access-trace questions at Q583; qualified profile retention already uses a generic source-focus definition.

findings.problem: The proposition says a named deletion operation, but bindings contain only fileId/systemId. Distinct deletion attempts on the same file during one interval can be accepted as independent records of the same operation.
findings.proposedRepair: Bind a deletion operation/event identity across origins, or require an assessed same-operation discriminator before independent validation; retain attempts and outcomes separately.

findings.problem: The base correctly covers presence and the three profiles separately cover deletion, lineage and unavailable metadata. They do not supply creation or execution-event definitions, and same-file/different-system follow-up has no explicit same-domain File discovery lead. Existing Host/Email pivots must not be advertised as that missing coverage.
findings.proposedRepair: Retain these as explicit scope limits. If creation, execution, parent revision or another-system file discovery is claimed, add separately qualified profiles/routes with full target identities, discovery references and no inherited target answer.
findings.scenario: A copied executable on host-B is a distinct File context; a recorded filename in process ancestry is neither proof of host-B bytes nor a file-creation event.

limits: No public graph question reviewed here authorizes a command/tool operation, approves organizational risk, determines financial/business loss, or attributes intent.
Presence, creation, execution, deletion, historical lineage, manifest digest equality and independently acquired byte equality must remain separate.
Accepted items are semantically acceptable only under their explicit binding/evidence prerequisites; this is not universal coverage, authentic-source validation or release/institutional approval.
